## The job

Drop three designer inputs that no renderer reads, so Studio stops publishing configuration that silently does nothing:

- `page:accordion` → `title`
- `page:accordion` → `items[].value`
- `page:header` → `icon`

## ⛔ Premise check first — this card is six days old and its baseline is stale

It was measured against `objectui@d8d0d66` on 2026-08-12, and the line numbers it quotes (`containers.tsx:793`, `:566`) **will** have moved. Re-derive all three verdicts against the current tree before deleting anything:

1. `PageAccordionRenderer` reads `items` / `allowMultiple` / `variant` and **not** `title`;
2. the accordion renderer **overwrites** `items[].value` with `panel-${idx}`, so an authored value can never reach the Radix item;
3. `page:header.icon` is retired from `@objectstack/spec` 17.0.0 and no renderer ever read it.

If any verdict no longer holds, **stop and report** rather than deleting on the card's authority. `premise_still_valid: false` with a partial or empty PR is a legitimate delivery.

## ⛔ The trap the card names explicitly — do not "fix" the sibling

**`page:tabs` is NOT the same case.** One component over, an authored `items[].value` **is** read (with a `tab-` fallback), which is why the spec declares it there. The accordion's is genuinely derived; the tabs one is genuinely live. A sweep that treats "`items[].value` is dead" as a general truth breaks tabs. Touch the accordion only.

## Zone 2 — PM notes (verify)

- `containers.tsx` is **read-only** for you: it is the evidence that the inputs are dead, not something to change. If you conclude a renderer *should* start reading one of these, that is the opposite direction — it needs a renderer read point first, and it is a different card. Report it, do not build it.
- The card's own framing is worth keeping: this is ADR-0078 on the **producer** side — an author configures a block in Studio, saves, sees no effect and gets no diagnostic. Deleting the inputs is what makes the designer honest.
- `page:header.icon` has an extra wrinkle worth a line in the PR body: because the spec closed these shapes, an authored `icon` is now **refused with a tombstone** (carrying an `os migrate meta --from 16` prescription) rather than silently stripped. So the designer is currently publishing an input whose value the platform actively tells the author to delete.

## Gates

Derive from your diff — expect `Lint`, `Type Check`, the test shards, changeset gates. Changeset required (`@object-ui/app-shell`). Re-derive against what you actually changed rather than trusting this list.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first line `Fixes #5212`. Push the branch early. Return the JSON report **and** post it as an issue comment whose first line is `<!-- os-dev-report -->`. Read the full issue body and every comment on GitHub yourself — note this card was **moved from `objectstack-ai/objectstack#7973`** today, and the original thread there has a comment that was not copied.

## The premise check earned its place — a third of this card was already done

The card listed three dead designer inputs. **`page:header.icon` had already been removed by #3829 / PR #4794 on 2026-08-16** — *two days after* the card's 2026-08-12 baseline was measured. So the card was describing a tree that no longer existed, and a dev working from the body alone would have gone looking for something that was not there.

Delivered: the two still-live inputs (`page:accordion.title`, `page:accordion.items[].value`). That is the whole of what remained, which is why `Fixes` rather than `Part of` is correct here.

**This is the third card today whose body was stale in a way that changed the work** — after #5195 (channel 2 was in a different file than the card, triage and my dispatch all said) and #3318 (ledger down from 29 rows to 1). I am recording the pattern rather than the individual cases: **in this repo the card body is the least current artifact, and the machine-readable one — the ledger, the registry, the test — is the truth.** My dispatches have been treating the body as a clue; that has been right three times today.

## Spot-checks

- **The `page:tabs` trap held.** One component over, an authored `items[].value` *is* read (with a `tab-` fallback), which is why the spec declares it there. The accordion's is genuinely derived — the renderer overwrites it with `panel-${idx}`. Tabs untouched, as instructed. A sweep that generalised "`items[].value` is dead" would have broken it.
- **Orphaned i18n keys removed too.** Deleting a designer input while leaving its label strings behind is how the *next* dead-key card gets filed; taking both in one change is the right radius.
- **A stale comment was corrected** — it used the accordion `value` as an ordering example, which stops being true with this change. Small, and exactly the kind of thing that rots into the next false premise.
- **Pins cover both sides**: the designer-side removal *and* the spec-side `unrecognized_keys` rejection, mirroring the existing `page:header.icon` pin. So an author who writes the removed key now meets a refusal rather than silence.

**Declared deviation, accepted and correctly handled:** the full `@object-ui/app-shell` lint queued behind the shared verify lock for 5+ minutes (held by another agent's vitest run). Per the reset instruction the dev abandoned the wait and ran `eslint` directly on the three changed files instead — 4 problems, 0 errors, all pre-existing `no-explicit-any` warnings outside this diff. CI's full lint is green above. **This is the behaviour I want under concurrency: narrow, declare, move on — not wait and stall.**

**On the stall:** this seat stalled once (backgrounding the queued lint and yielding) and was reset. It recovered without re-running anything. Recorded because the recovery was clean; the underlying trap is filed as objectstack#9687.

**No action on the dev's open question** — it flagged, correctly, that `page:header.icon` was fixed elsewhere and asked whether the original thread needs a note. It does not: the fact is stated in the PR body's premise-check section and now here, which is where an auditor of the three-item table will look.

Flipping out of draft and enqueueing.
